+# Unfinished intake files — source and receiving
+
+Scope: [Ledgerly #41](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/ledgerly/issues/41), estate-e3a41d2b3368 / source_work.
+
+The contribution adds explicit Save/Open/Replace for unfinished source and correction fields. Python validation, one-use reviewed revisions, the ordinary source-only draft path, Worker recovery and separate send approval retain their existing authority. [Usage and format](../../../web-demo/docs/intake-files.md).
+
+## Source witness and current composition
+
+The absence witness is actual commit `fba278f552e868ad2b94b7f1dc309eed6f1e8514`, tree `ddb2360a65b646a281969fea1abbb3238c154340`. The 43-file `baseline-source.json` capsule contains the complete original build closure: source, adapters, fixtures, package/lock, build configuration and source-embedded tests. All 43 Git blob hashes were independently recomputed from the exact bytes. The adjacent manifest records sizes, SHA-256 hashes and modes.
+
+The first historical receiving composition is based on actual parent `295153cc0c354415c39bcee7d2384412b4fa629f`, tree `599514b1ea0dc06edd0f8ed4acf7b1fdbbc49470`. This parent adds the client-receivables board. Its five main-module additions and entire panel are preserved. Our main delta is unchanged from its original reviewed form; the original absence witness stays frozen.
+
+The final native composition is based on actual parent `a4c7f05d511fb6e9ae4e357d78f696b464625ffc`, tree `d67d6d0479ea2fad0e4778365c6fcd06aa13edf6`. It preserves the optional rejection-reason owner’s current main, bridge, controls, CSS and tests. The intake main delta is identical; the existing VM harness adds only the two-method intake lifecycle port, and the browser receiver adds the two rejection modules to its preservation list without changing assertions.
+
+Publication must use a freshly read real parent and preserve every other parent blob and mode. No synthetic local ancestry belongs in the adoption branch.
+
+## Historical accepted core evidence
+
+`author-native/native-core-v1.json` records the original Mac receiving run on Node 26.3.0: 11 groups, 59 assertions and unchanged source hashes. It executes the TypeScript codec through native type erasure, strict admission, raw value preservation and byte/line boundaries, and parses the candidate source. The process's exit code 0 was separately observed.
+
+The retained harness has its original isolated Mac paths. Its result qualifies the frozen codec and syntax, not TypeScript semantic build, DOM behavior or the Python Worker. The report was retained from the exact successful process JSON; its historical main/index pins precede current receivables composition.
+
+The root reviewer inspected codec, UI, original review renderer, current main delta and all browser-driver assertions. It requested no runtime change. The source-only contract was clarified explicitly: fresh valid extraction retains the ordinary explicit raw draft; restored correction fields require fresh human confirmation and a one-use review.
+
+## Current project and browser receiving
+
+The existing browser-engine CI job installs the declared lock, runs Vitest with actual Pyodide, and builds with TypeScript/Vite. Its additive step runs `web-demo/tools/check_intake_file_browser.mjs` with installed Chrome. No new browser package, dependency or workflow is introduced.
+
+The browser driver receives original page loss; actual file download/reopen; invalid and valid Python review; retired authority; unchanged current invoices/pending approvals during replacement; malformed/oversize/UTF-8/editor-loss refusal; stale reads and cancellation; explicit Worker failure/restart; both source-only validity outcomes; literal text; trusted keyboard activation; and narrow layout. It retains actual Worker requests/results, file bytes, screenshots and source/build hashes before and after.
+
+The Worker observer copies real replies and never substitutes an extraction or validation result. One control holds a real reply before an explicitly authored terminal error. Delayed-file controls call the browser's original File method when released. These fault controls remain labelled separately from normal behavior.
+
+The first native full test run and build are preserved separately. The build passed. Tests reported 105 passes, four missing intake lifecycle bindings in the existing VM harness, one omitted receiving fixture, and four unchanged 10-second Pyodide hook timeouts with 12 workers. The correction adds only a two-method intake UI port to the existing VM globals, preserving every assertion; actual file/DOM behavior stays in the browser receiver. The existing root overdue fixture is recovered at its exact parent blob. Native reruns bound worker count without raising timeouts.
+
+The bounded second full run on the 295 composition reported **110 passed, 21 skipped, four unchanged 10-second Pyodide suite-hook timeouts, exit 1**. All 31 new codec cases and all five recovery cases passed; the recovered overdue fixture ran six native contracts successfully. This is a retained partial result, not a full-suite pass.
+
+On the final a4 composition, the native TypeScript/Vite build passed, the existing recovery suite passed **5/5**, and the current owner’s Python rejection suite passed **6/6**. All 75 recorded source inputs remained unchanged during that receiving. Receipt documentation was finalized afterward; no runtime or evaluator bytes changed.
+
+Native browser admission stopped when `/snap/bin/chromium --version` exceeded 15 seconds. No application browser was launched. The observed process error is retained separately; the admission script failed before writing its intended metadata file. **Hosted full CI and the actual Chrome intake receiver remain required before merge.** This packet is ready for a draft qualification PR, not deployment.
+
+Each receiving attempt has a distinct new directory/log. Failures are retained with exact source/driver hashes. A dependency install, source checkpoint or parse pass is never labelled as a browser/CI/merge result.
+
+## Resource history
+
+Initial Mac staging/core receiving succeeded. Later file-API and native guarded writes encountered ENOSPC; dependent work stopped. Subsequent read-only Mac requests timed out without a PID/result. No uncertain filesystem action or browser launch was replayed.
+
+The full source/capsule checkpoint was recovered into a new isolated ThinkPad directory after transport and capacity returned. The exact declared lock was installed only there, with unchanged lock hash. These observations do not establish a cause for the host capacity failures.
+
+The qualification manifest records accepted current runs and remaining gates. Source qualification, publication, merge and live deployment are distinct states.

+# Hosted qualification of unfinished intake files
+
+This receipt qualifies Ledgerly PR #48 head `30dbdddabdc4db272e21ebbb9363270b4438fd32`, built by GitHub Actions at virtual merge `3502693543169ebed3ebe97d1954b63d99421ee7` over actual parent `a4c7f05d511fb6e9ae4e357d78f696b464625ffc`. Both published head and tested virtual merge have the exact same tree, `1222b5b20efa2b6ced4d885b2a1c3649e860ed17`.
+
+[Workflow run](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/ledgerly/actions/runs/37830909640) completed successfully. Python core passed 343 tests plus 126 subtests. All 131 Vitest tests passed, TypeScript/Vite built, and the existing CSV, invoice-record and client-receivables browser checks passed. The new actual Chrome 154.0.8037.97 intake receiver passed nine groups and 405 assertions, including the original page-loss witness, real file downloads and reopens, fresh Python checks, stale-read retirement, failed replacement and Worker restart, current invoice/approval preservation, source-only behavior, trusted keyboard actions and mobile layout. All 54 recorded source hashes match the current qualification; source and build remained unchanged, and Chrome exited normally.
+
+`receiving-report.json` is the exact report recovered from the job's bounded log bundle. `receiving-bundle.json.gz.b64` retains the exact gzip archive in a text-safe form. Base64-decode it, check gzip SHA-256 `89e382d912ccf1fa3af7abc7ae1c00197b1549403bbee26dc0023de1cd7d7671`, gunzip its JSON and verify each member's byte count and SHA-256 before extracting. All 11 non-image members were verified; the full member list is adjacent. Actual Worker requests/replies and downloaded file bytes are inside the archive. Authored failure/hold controls remain explicitly labelled in the report.
+
+Screenshots remain in [GitHub artifact 11573162715](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/ledgerly/actions/runs/37830909640/artifacts/11573162715), originally scheduled to expire on 2026-10-22. Their hashes are in the report. The documented connector returned a reusable ZIP reference, but the single local materialization request returned HTTP 403 before any bytes; no local screenshot recovery is claimed and no alternate route was attempted.
+
+The earlier native partial suites and browser-version timeout remain historical failures in the parent receipt directory. This successful hosted receiving does not relabel them. This evidence does not itself claim merge or live rollout. The published 33-file manifest records the complete tree/preservation gate and the final documentation-link-only correction from the frozen native packet.
+
+The independent rejection-owner composition review found no source blocker. The existing approval click-handler (762 bytes) and complete `renderState` body (2,327 bytes), plus rejection controls/CSS, bridge, approval preview, Worker/client and owner test/driver blobs are unchanged from a4. Its source-level conclusion is that notes keyed by stable pending action IDs survive successful or failed analysis; busy disables approval/rejection and explicit restart clears those IDs under the existing contract. The 405-assertion browser trace contains no rejection calls or typed-note controls. A typed-note → intake replacement → reject flow was not executed; source review and browser coverage remain distinct.

+# Continue an unfinished invoice intake
+
+Use **Save intake** below the invoice intake to download the source email and any current correction fields. You can save while values are incomplete: an empty quantity, an unfinished recipient or a price Python will later reject stays as typed. Saving runs no Python check and creates no invoice.
+
+The browser prepares a file named like `ledgerly-intake-20261008T160000000Z.json`. Keep the downloaded file to continue in another visit. Ledgerly does not automatically save or recover a closed page.
+
+## Reopen and review
+
+1. Choose **Open intake** and select a saved file.
+2. Review its filename, saved time, recipient, line count and source preview. The preview shows the first 2,000 characters; replacement loads the complete source and all saved fields.
+3. Save the current intake first if you also need those edits. **Keep current intake** or Escape leaves the current intake unchanged.
+4. Load the local Python engine if necessary, then choose **Replace current intake**. Python analyzes the saved source before the editor restores its saved fields.
+
+Opening is only a preview. Explicit replacement changes the current source and corrections. Current sandbox invoices, pending approvals and the clock remain separate.
+
+### Files with correction fields
+
+Saved correction fields reopen unchecked. The original warnings from the new source analysis remain above the form, including warnings resolved by a supplied correction such as a missing recipient.
+
+Read the warnings, confirm the fields, and choose **Check corrected fields with Python**. Only a new valid review creates a one-use revision for **Create reviewed sandbox draft**. The file restores no earlier review identifier or confirmation.
+
+That draft's send still appears in the existing human approval gate. Reopening, checking or downloading an intake never approves it.
+
+### Source-only files
+
+If no correction form exists when you save, the file records only source text. Replacing from that file runs a new Python extraction and keeps the ordinary source-analysis behavior:
+
+- Invalid or low-confidence extraction remains blocked.
+- Valid new extraction enables the existing explicit **Create sandbox draft** action.
+- The draft's send still needs separate approval.
+
+A source-only file invents no human review and restores no earlier extraction result. Editing the correction form follows the usual human review path.
+
+## Interrupted work
+
+If incoming source analysis fails, the previous source and correction fields stay in the editor. Their prior review is retired; confirm and check them again before drafting.
+
+If the Python Worker stops, **Save intake** remains available for retained input when no action is busy. The existing **Restart empty sandbox** action starts a new in-memory ledger and preserves the editor's input. A later explicit correction check reanalyzes the retained source in the new session. Intake files never replay interrupted actions.
+
+## Format and limits
+
+Version 1 is UTF-8 JSON with exactly these outer keys:
+
+```json
+{
+  "format": "ledgerly-intake",
+  "version": 1,
+  "saved_at": "2026-10-08T16:00:00.000Z",
+  "source_text": "Fictional job email...",
+  "review_fields": null
+}
+```
+
+When present, `review_fields` has exactly `client_name`, `client_email`, `due_days`, `amount_paid` and `line_items`. The first four values are raw strings. Each line contains raw string values for `desc`, `qty`, `unit_price`, `currency` and `unit`.
+
+The saved time is an exact UTC timestamp describing file preparation; it establishes no invoice validity. Files are limited to 2 MiB and 200 editable lines. Missing/extra fields, unsupported versions, malformed JSON, invalid UTF-8 and numeric values in raw-string fields are refused. Imported strings the existing editor would silently alter are also refused, including carriage-return source text and line values that cannot survive the existing escaped renderer.
+
+Invoice, approval, payment, clock, sandbox ledger, confidence, checked revision and confirmation state are excluded. Existing invoice-record and ledger downloads remain separate features.
+
+## Development receiving
+
+From `web-demo`, run the normal project commands and use an installed Chrome:
+
+```sh
+npm ci
+npm test
+npm run build
+node tools/check_intake_file_browser.mjs --browser /path/to/chrome --output /path/to/new/receiving-directory --emit-bundle
+```
+
+The receiver uses Node's built-in Chrome DevTools transport. It builds the frozen original application privately using the same locked dependencies, then exercises both original and current applications through the real Python Worker. The output directory must be new.
+
+See the [source and receiving record](../../docs/receipts/intake-files-e3a41d2b3368-20261008/README.md) for exact boundaries, source pins, reports and historical failures.
